 Judgment

This is petition filed under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act, seeking compensation of Rs.10,00,000/- from the respondents, on account of grievous injuries sustained by the petitioner in a road traffic accident.

2. The brief facts of the case are as follows:
On 15-06-2023 at about 5:45 a.m., the petitioner was traveling in SRS Bus bearing No.KA-51-AG-1257.
From the starting point of the journey the driver of the said bus was driving the bus at high speed, in rash and negligent MVC No.6946/2023 manner.

When the said bus was proceeding on NH-48 road, near DNDS Chowltry,
Kyathasandra, Tumakuru, due to over speed the driver of the bus lost control over the said vehicle and dashed to a tipper lorry, which was proceeding ahead of the bus on the correct side of the road.
Due to said impact, the petitioner has sustained severe injuries to her right ankle.

Immediately after the accident, she was shifted to Tumkur Government Hospital, wherein she took first aid treatment and then she was shifted to Meditech Speciality Hospital, Bengaluru, wherein she took treatment as an in- patient.
Earlier to the accident, she was working as H.R. (Human Resources) at Mechstore Adofil, Bengaluru and earning Rs.30,000/- per month.
But, due to the accidental injuries, she became permanently disabled and thereby lost her earning capacity.
The Tumakuru Traffic Police have registered the case against the driver of the said bus for the offence punishable under Section 279 and 338 of I.P.C.
The respondent No.1 is the insurer and respondent No.2 is the MVC No.6946/2023 owner of the offending vehicle.
Hence, they are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioner.
Therefore, it is prayed to allow the petition and award compensation of Rs.10,00,000/- with interest.
3. On service of notice to the respondents, the respondent No.1 has appeared through its counsel and filed its written statement.
Whereas, the respondent No.2 did not choose to appear and remained absent.

Hence, the respondent No.2 is placed as ex-parte.

sentences.text: 4. The respondent No.1 in its written statement has denied all the allegations made in the petition.
It has admitted the issuance of insurance policy in respect of SRS Bus bearing No. KA-51-AG-1257 and its validity as on the date of accident.
It has denied the involvement of the bus bearing No.KA-51-AG-1257 in the alleged accident.

Further it is contended that, the accident occurred due to rash and negligent act on the part of the driver of the tipper lorry MVC No.6946/2023 which was proceeding ahead of the bus and negligence of the petitioner also.
It has further contended that, the petition is bad for non-joinder of necessary parties i.e., the insured and insurer of the tipper lorry which was proceeding ahead of the bus.
It has denied the age, income and avocation of the petitioner, injuries, medical expenses and treatment taken by her.
The compensation claimed is highly excessive and exorbitant.
It has contended that, the petition is bad for non compliance of provision under Section 158(6) of Motor Vehicles Act.

It has further contended that, the driver of the offending bus was not holding valid and effective driving licence and the bus was not having valid fitness certificate and permit, at the time of accident.
Further, it has sought for permission to contest even on behalf of respondent No.2 under Section 170 of the Motor Vehicles Act.
It seeks protection under Section 147 and 149 of Motor Vehicles Act.
For the above stated denials and contentions, it prayed for dismissal of the petition.

On the basis of rival pleadings of both the sides, the following issues are framed:
ISSUES

1 . Whether the petitioner proves that, she has sustained grievous injuries in a road traffic accident, alleged to have occurred on 15-06-2023 at about 5:45 p.m., due to the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the SRS Bus bearing registration No.KA- 51-AG-1257?
2.
Whether the petitioner is entitled for compensation?
If so, what is the quantum and from whom?

3 . What order or Award?

On the other hand, the respondent No.1 has not adduced any evidence on its behalf.

11. On meticulously going through the above police documents marked as Ex.P.1 to 9, prima-facia it reveals that, the accident in question has taken place due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of offending SRS Bus bearing No.KA-51-AG-1257 and dashing the same to an ongoing tipper lorry from behind.
Further it reveals that, due to said impact the petitioner has sustained grievous injury on her right ankle.

The investigation officer in his final MVC No.6946/2023 report, which is marked as Ex.P.9, has clearly stated that, due to rash and negligent driving of the offending SRS Bus bearing Reg. No. KA-51-AG-1257 the said accident has taken place and the petitioner has sustained grievous injuries.

12. At the outset, it is pertinent to note that, in the present case, the date, time and place of accident,
involvement of offending SRS Bus bearing No.KA-51-AG- 1257 in the alleged accident, issuance of insurance policy by the respondent No.1 in respect of said vehicle and its validity as on the date of accident, is not in dispute.

Further, the above oral and documentary evidence placed on record by the petitioner has remained undisputed by the owner of offending vehicle/respondent No.2, as he did not choose to appear and contest the case of petitioner.

Whereas, the respondent No.1 insurance company, though has denied the said facts in its written statement and taken specific defence that,

sentences.text: The respondent No.1 has neither adduced any evidence to establish the said contention or produced any rebuttal evidence to disprove the oral and documentary evidence placed on record by the petitioner.

There is absolutely no evidence placed on record by the respondent to show that, accident in question has taken place due to negligence act on the part of the driver of the tipper lorry which was proceeding ahead of the bus and negligence of the petitioner.

Further, the petitioner/P.W.1, has unequivocally denied the suggestion made in her cross- examination that, the accident in question is not caused due to rash and negligent driving of the SRS Bus bearing No.KA-51-AG-1257 and the injuries sustained by her are due to her own negligence

Though, the learned counsel for respondent No.1 has cross-examined P.W.1 in length, MVC No.6946/2023 nothing worth has been elicited from her mouth which creates doubt on the veracity of her evidence.

13. Further, the Ex.P.4 spot mahazer and Ex.P.6 sketch also clearly speaks that, the said accident has taken place on left side of 100 feet wide Tumkur-Bengaluru NH-48 road, near D.N.D.S. Chowltry at Kyathasandra, Tumkur, due to dashing of offending SRS Bus bearing No.KA-51-AG-1257 to an ongoing tipper lorry.

Further, as per the Motor Vehicle Accident Report, which is marked as Ex.P.7,
the accident is not caused due to any mechanical defects in the vehicle involved in the accident.

When the accident was not caused due to the any mechanical defects in the offending vehicle and there was no negligence on the part of the unknown ongoing tipper lorry, then in the present facts and circumstances of the case, it can be presumed that, the said accident had occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of offending vehicle.

There is absolutely no rebuttal evidence placed on record by the respondent No.1 MVC No.6946/2023 and even nothing has been elicited in the cross- examination of P.W.1 to show that, the said accident has occurred due to negligence on the part of the driver of ongoing tipper lorry or there was any contributory negligence on his part in the cause of accident.

In such circumstances, there is no impediment to believe the final report filed by the investigation officer and other police records, with regard to date, time and place of accident,
involvement of the offending vehicle, rash and negligent driving of the rider of offending vehicle and injuries caused to the petitioner in the said accident.

14. Further, on meticulously going through the Ex.P.8 wound certificate, Ex.P.10 CT Scan reports,
Ex.P.12 and 21 OPD records and Ex.P.21 x-ray, it clearly reveals that, the petitioner has suffered grievous injuries in a road traffic accident and she has suffered fracture of anteriolateral margin of calcaneal right.
The same has been deposed by the P.W.2, who is the doctor who has clinically examined the MVC No.6946/2023 petitioner and assessed the disability to the petitioner.
On the other hand, there is no rebuttal evidence produced by the respondent No.1 to show that, the above medical records produced by the petitioner are false created documents.

15. Further, it is well settled principle of law that, in a case relating to the Motor Accident Claims,
the claimants are not required to prove the case as required to be done in a criminal trial.

The Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Parameshwari V/s Amir Chand and others, reported in (2011)
SCC 635, has clearly held that, "in a road accident claim cases the strict principle of proof in a Uma B H vs New India Ass Co Ltd on 8 January, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/104515532/
5 criminal case are not required."

Therefore, in the light of observations made in the above cited decisions and for the above stated reasons, this Court is of the considered opinion that, the petitioner has successfully proved through cogent and corroborative evidence that, she has sustained grievous injuries in a road traffic accident,
occurred on 15-06-2023 at about 5.45 a.m., on NH-48 road, near DNDS Chowltry at Kyathasandra,
Tumakuru, due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of SRS Bus bearing Reg. No.
KA-51-AG-1257.
Hence, I answer Issue No.1 in Affirmative.
18. Issue No.2:

While answering above issue this Court has come to conclusion that, the petitioner has successfully proved through cogent and corroborative evidence that, MVC No.6946/2023 the accident is caused due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of offending SRS Bus bearing Reg.
No. KA-51-AG- 1257 and she has sustained grievous injury on her right ankle.
As per the medical records placed on record by the petitioner, she has sustained fracture of anteriolateral margin of calcaneal right and for the said injury she has undergone surgery.
Therefore, this Court is of the further opinion that, the petitioner is entitled for compensation under various heads.

The damages are to be assessed under two heads i.e. pecuniary damages, such as medical treatment, attendants,
transport, actual loss of earning, future loss of earning etc., and non pecuniary damages, such as mental and physical shock, loss of amenities, loss of expectation of life, loss of prospects of marriage etc.,

The petitioner is entitled for compensation under the following heads:
i) Towards loss of future income: In order to determine the compensation towards loss of future income, MVC No.6946/2023 the age, monthly income and disability of the petitioner are to be determined.
To prove her age, the petitioner has produced the copy of her Aadhar card, which is marked as Ex.P.13.
As per Ex.P.13, the date of birth of the petitioner is 21-08-1992.
The accident has taken place on 15-06-2023 at about 5.45 P.M.
Therefore, the age of the petitioner as on the date of accident is considered as 31 years.

Further, the P.W.2, who is the doctor who has examined the petitioner for the purpose of assessment of disability, has clearly deposed in his examination-in-chief affidavit that, on clinical examination he found that, the petitioner has suffered fracture of anteriolateral margin of calcaneal right.

Further he has deposed that, on clinical and radiological examination of injuries suffered by the petitioner he found that, the petitioner has suffered 28% physical disability of right lower limb and 9% physical disability to the whole body of the petitioner.
The oral evidence of P.W.2 is fully corroborated with documentary evidence.

The Ex.P.8 MVC No.6946/2023 wound certificate, Ex.P.10 CT Scan reports, Ex.P.12 and 21 OPD records and Ex.P.21 X-ray, clearly speaks that, the petitioner has suffered grievous injuries in a road traffic accident and she has suffered fracture of anteriolateral Uma B H vs New India Ass Co Ltd on 8 January, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/104515532/

Though, the learned counsel for respondent No.1 has cross-examined P.W.2 in length, nothing worth has been elicited from his mouth which creates doubt on the veracity of his evidence.
Further, he has clearly denied the suggestions made to him that, there is no disability to the petitioner and he has exaggerated the percentage of disability to the petitioner.

But, it is pertinent to note that, the P.W.2 has deposed in his evidence that, the accident has occurred on 15-06-2023 and he has assessed the disability to the petitioner on 10-07-2024, which is after lapse of one year from the date of injuries caused to the petitioner.
Further he has deposed that, X-ray of ankle shows both fracture malunited with osteoarthtitis subtalar joint and have difficulty to do her day today activities.

But, MVC No.6946/2023 the P.W.2 has clearly admitted in his cross-examination that, as per X-ray report issued by Care Hospital, the petitioner has not sustained any fracture, as per CT scan report the petitioner has sustained small anterior lateral marginal fracture of calcaneum.

The petitioner has not at all admitted in the hospital, the petitioner has not undergone any surgery for the injuries alleged to have been sustained to her, only conservative treatment has been provided to the petitioner.

Therefore, in such circumstances, taking into consideration the age of the petitioner,
injuries sustained by her, duration of treatment and the oral and documentary evidence on record, this Court is of the opinion that, considering the physical disability of 3% to the whole body of the petitioner would be justified.
Hence, in the instant case the physical disability of 3% to the whole body of the petitioner is considered.
a) The petitioner has deposed in her evidence that, before accident she was working as H.R. (Human MVC No.6946/2023 Resources) at Mechstore Adofil, Bengaluru and earning Rs.30,000/- per month.
Further, she has deposed that, due to grievous injuries suffered in the said accident she is unable to do her work.
The respondent No.1 has specifically denied the same.
In such circumstances, the burden was on the petitioner to prove her avocation and income.

To substantiate the same she has produced salary slips (total 3), job offer letter, statement of accounts given by ICICI Bank and Karnataka Bank,
which are marked as Ex.P.14 to 17.

The said documents clearly establishes that, before accident the petitioner was working as H.R. (Human Resources) and Admin Executive, at Mechstore Adofil,
Bengaluru and she was getting salary of Rs.29,800/- per month.

Hence, the monthly income of the petitioner is considered as Rs.29,800/- per month and the annual income of the petitioner as Rs.3,57,600/-.
b)

As per the ratio laid down in the case of Sarla Verma and others V/s Delhi Transport Corporation and MVC No.6946/2023 another, reported in 2009 ACJ 1298, the appropriate multiplier for a person whose is aged about 31 years is 16.

The petitioner has deposed that, she has incurred expenses of Rs.40,000/-
towards treatment, medicine, conveyance etc.
In order to prove the same, she has produced 10 medical bills, as per Ex.P.18.
All the bills have been examined carefully and found that the petitioner has spent total amount of Rs.13,157/- towards medical expenses.
Therefore, the petitioner is entitled for Rs.13,157/- under the head of medical expenses.
iii) Pain and sufferings:
In the present case, the petitioner has sustained fracture of anteriolateral margin of calcaneal right.
Admittedly, for the said injury the petitioner has undergone conservative treatment.
As per the evidence of P.W.2, the said injury has caused physical MVC No.6946/2023 disability to the petitioner.
In such circumstances, certainly the petitioner would have suffered pain and sufferings.

Therefore, taking into considering the injuries sustained and disability to the petitioner, this Court is of the opinion that, an compensation amount of Rs.20,000/- is to be awarded to the petitioner towards pain and sufferings.

iv) Attendant charges: As per the medical records available on record the petitioner has sustained fracture of anteriolateral margin of calcaneal right and she has undergone conservative treatment for the said injury.
She might have spent considerable amount towards attendant charges during the treatment period.
But, the petitioner has not stated anything with regard to treatment period or for how many days she has undergone treatment and even there is no document produced by her with respect to same.
Therefore, in such circumstances, this Court is of the opinion that, awarding compensation of Rs.4,000/- towards the attendant charges would be justified.

sentences.text: viii) Loss of amenities:

It is evident from the documents placed on record that, as on the date of accident the age of the petitioner was 31 years and unfortunately she has suffered fracture of anteriolateral margin of calcaneal right in the road traffic accident.
The evidence shows that, she has suffered permanent disability to the MVC No.6946/2023 extent of 3% to the whole body.

Therefore,
awarding compensation of Rs.10,000/- towards loss of amenities would be just and reasonable.
ix) Future medical expenses:
The P.W.2 has not stated anything with regard to requirement of any further treatment to the petitioner and future medical expenses.
In such circumstances, the question of awarding future medical expenses does not arise at all.
Therefore, no compensation is awarded in this particular head.

In all, the petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.2,56,605/- with interest at the rate of 6% per annum, from the date of petition till its realization.
20. Liability:
Admittedly, as on the date of accident, the respondent No.1 is the insurer and respondent No.2 is the owner of the offending vehicle.

Further, the evidence placed on record by the petitioner clearly establishes that, due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of offending vehicle bearing Reg. No.KA-51-AG-1257 the accident has occurred.
In such circumstances, the respondent No.2 being the owner of said vehicle is vicariously liable to compensate for the damages caused by the said vehicle.
The respondent No.1 being the insurer of the vehicle has to indemnify the respondent No.2.

Therefore, the respondent No.1 and 2 are jointly and severally liable to pay the Uma B H vs New India Ass Co Ltd on 8 January, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/104515532/
9 compensation to the MVC No.6946/2023 petitioner.

sentences.text: However, the primary liability is on the respondent No.1 to pay the compensation to the petitioner.

Therefore, for the above stated reasons,
holding that, the petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.2,56,605/- from the respondent No.1,
I answer Issue No.2 in Partly Affirmative.
21. Issue No.3:
In view of the above findings, I proceed to pass the following order:
ORDER The petition is partly allowed with costs.

The petitioner is entitled to compensation of Rs.2,56,605/- (Rupees two lakh fifty six thousand six hundred and five only) with interest at the rate of 6% p.a., from the date of petition till realisation.
The respondents are jointly and severally liable to pay the above compensation amount.

However, the MVC No.6946/2023 primary liability to pay the compensation amount is fastened on respondent No.1 - Insurance Company and it is directed to pay the compensation amount within two months from the date of this order.
The entire compensation amount with proportionate interest shall be released in favour of the petitioner through e-payment on proper identification and verification.
Advocate's fee is fixed at Rs.2,000/-.
Draw award accordingly.

opennyai_summary.arguments:
It has contended that, the petition is bad for non compliance of provision under Section 158(6) of Motor Vehicles Act.
It has further contended that, the driver of the offending bus was not holding valid and effective driving licence and the bus was not having valid fitness certificate and permit, at the time of accident.
Further, it has sought for permission to contest even on behalf of respondent No.2 under Section 170 of the Motor Vehicles Act.
It seeks protection under Section 147 and 149 of Motor Vehicles Act.
The petitioner has deposed that, she has incurred expenses of Rs.40,000/-
towards treatment, medicine, conveyance etc.
opennyai_summary.issue:
1 . Whether the petitioner proves that, she has sustained grievous injuries in a road traffic accident, alleged to have occurred on 15-06-2023 at about 5:45 p.m., due to the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the SRS Bus bearing registration No.KA- 51-AG-1257?
2.
Whether the petitioner is entitled for compensation?
If so, what is the quantum and from whom?
3 . What order or Award?

opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
12. At the outset, it is pertinent to note that, in the present case, the date, time and place of accident,
involvement of offending SRS Bus bearing No.KA-51-AG- 1257 in the alleged accident, issuance of insurance policy by the respondent No.1 in respect of said vehicle and its validity as on the date of accident, is not in dispute.
Whereas, the respondent No.1 insurance company, though has denied the said facts in its written statement and taken specific defence that,
Uma B H vs New India Ass Co Ltd on 8 January, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/104515532/
4 SRS Bus bearing No.KA-51-AG-1257 is not at all involved in the alleged accident and the said accident MVC No.6946/2023 has occurred due to negligence act on the part of the driver of the tipper lorry which was proceeding ahead of the bus and negligence of the petitioner, it has failed to prove the said contentions.
The respondent No.1 has neither adduced any evidence to establish the said contention or produced any rebuttal evidence to disprove the oral and documentary evidence placed on record by the petitioner.
There is absolutely no evidence placed on record by the respondent to show that, accident in question has taken place due to negligence act on the part of the driver of the tipper lorry which was proceeding ahead of the bus and negligence of the petitioner.
When the accident was not caused due to the any mechanical defects in the offending vehicle and there was no negligence on the part of the unknown ongoing tipper lorry, then in the present facts and circumstances of the case, it can be presumed that, the said accident had occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of offending vehicle.
There is absolutely no rebuttal evidence placed on record by the respondent No.1 MVC No.6946/2023 and even nothing has been elicited in the cross- examination of P.W.1 to show that, the said accident has occurred due to negligence on the part of the driver of ongoing tipper lorry or there was any contributory negligence on his part in the cause of accident.
In such circumstances, there is no impediment to believe the final report filed by the investigation officer and other police records, with regard to date, time and place of accident,
involvement of the offending vehicle, rash and negligent driving of the rider of offending vehicle and injuries caused to the petitioner in the said accident.
On the other hand, there is no rebuttal evidence produced by the respondent No.1 to show that, the above medical records produced by the petitioner are false created documents.
15. Further, it is well settled principle of law that, in a case relating to the Motor Accident Claims,
the claimants are not required to prove the case as required to be done in a criminal trial.
16. The Hon'ble Supreme Court, in the case of Bimla Devi and others V/s Himachal Road Transport Corporation and others, reported in (2009) 13 SCC 513, has clearly held that, "in a case relating to the Motor Accident Claims, the MVC No.6946/2023 claimants are merely required to establish their case on touch stone of preponderance of probability and the standard of proof on beyond reasonable doubt could not be applied."
The petitioner is entitled for compensation under the following heads:
i) Towards loss of future income: In order to determine the compensation towards loss of future income, MVC No.6946/2023 the age, monthly income and disability of the petitioner are to be determined.
Therefore, in such circumstances, taking into consideration the age of the petitioner,
injuries sustained by her, duration of treatment and the oral and documentary evidence on record, this Court is of the opinion that, considering the physical disability of 3% to the whole body of the petitioner would be justified.
Hence, in the instant case the physical disability of 3% to the whole body of the petitioner is considered.
In the present case, the petitioner has sustained fracture of anteriolateral margin of calcaneal right.
In such circumstances, certainly the petitioner would have suffered pain and sufferings.
Therefore, taking into considering the injuries sustained and disability to the petitioner, this Court is of the opinion that, an compensation amount of Rs.20,000/- is to be awarded to the petitioner towards pain and sufferings.
Therefore, in such circumstances, this Court is of the opinion that, awarding compensation of Rs.4,000/- towards the attendant charges would be justified.
But, the petitioner has not stated anything with regard to treatment period or for how many days she has undergone treatment and even there is no document produced by her with respect to same.
Therefore, in such circumstances, this Court is of the opinion that, awarding compensation of Rs.4,000/- towards the food and nourishment charges would be justified.

21. Issue No.3:
In view of the above findings, I proceed to pass the following order:
ORDER The petition is partly allowed with costs.
The petitioner is entitled to compensation of Rs.2,56,605/- (Rupees two lakh fifty six thousand six hundred and five only) with interest at the rate of 6% p.a., from the date of petition till realisation.
The respondents are jointly and severally liable to pay the above compensation amount.
However, the MVC No.6946/2023 primary liability to pay the compensation amount is fastened on respondent No.1 - Insurance Company and it is directed to pay the compensation amount within two months from the date of this order.
The entire compensation amount with proportionate interest shall be released in favour of the petitioner through e-payment on proper identification and verification.
Advocate's fee is fixed at Rs.2,000/-.
Draw award accordingly.
